checks.label: Energy balance (deposited = stored + rejected, from the outputs)
checks.note: all 10 slices pass; the worst is slice 1 of 10 (height 0.0191 m): largest relative gap over the outputs; threshold 16.2% of the largest of the energy deposited, rejected and stored anywhere in the run (a boundary history: the energies can cross zero, and the heat leaving can change within a few steps between outputs). It includes the first-order error of depositing the source at the new time (about 1/N of the energy over a ramp of N steps) and a trapezoid over the output times for the heat leaving

checks.label: OFFBEAT vs the independent finite-volume solution (max cell deviation)
checks.note: all 10 slices pass; the worst is slice 1 of 10 (height 0.0191 m): largest at t = 59.99999999999873 s; bound 14.289 K = min(3 x 0.016 K [the independent solution's own change when its cells are halved], 0.5% of the peak rise) + 0.02 K + 14.2 K for the heat flow along the pin (an axial stack)

checks.label: Time-stepping error of the peak temperature (step vs half step)
checks.note: all 10 slices pass; the worst is slice 5 of 10 (height 0.1715 m): the peak changes by at most 0.149 K, at any step of the run, when the step is halved; threshold 2% of the peak rise (12.53 K). With a boundary history every cell and the outer wall are compared at each output too: at most 0.169 K, threshold 2% of the largest excursion of any cell (11.22 K). If it fails, shorten the time step

checks.label: Energy balance of the whole pin (deposited = stored + rejected, summed over the slices)
checks.note: the slices' energies summed; threshold 3% of the largest energy exchanged anywhere in the run. The end faces carry no heat, so the heat flow along the pin cancels in the sum and no allowance for it is made here

checks.label: Axial heat flow allowed for in the per-slice tolerances
checks.note: the steady estimate is 0.134 % of the largest rise (src/core/axial.ts); the per-slice cross-check is widened by 3 times it as a fraction of the largest rise of any slice (2.52 K), and the per-slice energy balance by 3 times it as a fraction of the slice's own power (the end slices make little heat and take a larger share). A transient's axial flow is not larger than the steady one for the same shape, but it was measured on the real solver only in the tests of docs/axial-stack.md. The heat the slices can exchange along the height during the run is bounded from the independent solutions (up to 14.2 K and 13.2 % of a slice's energy; the steady estimate does not bound a run in which the coolant cannot carry the heat away). The exchange number (rate x run time) is 0.0628, below 1, where the bound held on the real solver: each slice's allowance is the larger of the two

thermalOnly: Thermal-only result. It says nothing about stress, failure or fuel integrity. One through-thickness solution per axial slice of the plate, with the heat flow along the height that the solver includes. The checks compare each slice with its own one-dimensional slab closed form within a bound that includes an estimate of that heat flow.
